podcast.title: Early Origins with Joe Meek
podcast.body: Songs such as "Night of the Vampire" by The Demon Trackers and "Till the Fall of the Wind Knight" by Screaming Lord Sutch, both meticulously produced by Joe Meek, are identified as some of the earliest examples of what would later become known as Gothic Rock. These tracks vividly showcased Meek's profound fascination with dark and esoteric themes. "siendo una de las primeras muestras de lo que luego sería conocido como Roc Gotico."

srcs.episode: El productor que escuchó el nuevo mundo. Joe Meek.

podcast.title: Gothic Rock Lineage – From Tambora's Eruption to Mary Shelley to Bauhaus
podcast.body: The genealogy of gothic rock traces back to the 1815 eruption of the Tambora volcano in Indonesia — the largest in recorded history — which caused the "Year Without a Summer" in 1816. The resulting gloom and cold inspired Mary Shelley to conceive *Frankenstein*, a foundational text of Gothic literature. That Gothic tradition, running through horror cinema and theatrical glamour of the 1960s, was eventually absorbed into rock music by bands like Bauhaus, Joy Division, and The Cure in the late 1970s. "The eruption of the Tambora volcano in 1815 caused the 'Year Without Summer' in 1816, inspiring Mary Shelley to conceive 'Frankenstein,' a cornerstone of Gothic literature."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influences
podcast.body: Gothic rock draws its "DNA" from 1960s psychedelia, with influences extending back to The Velvet Underground and Leonard Cohen from the 1960s. Additionally, Alice Cooper's death-obsessed shock rock of the early 1970s and certain elements of David Bowie's work are credited as contributing to the genre's development. "Gothrock has some DNA from 60's psych, but its influences go as far back as the velvet underground, and even some Leonard Cohen from the 1960's."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Literary Influences and Atmosphere
podcast.body: Bands in this genre, often referred to as "the darks," were influenced by authors like Kafka, Dostoevsky, and Baudelaire, creating heavy and melancholic atmospheres in their music. "los que leían a Cazca, Dostallezki o Valar. Y creaban atmósferas pesadas y melancólicas."

srcs.episode: La traición que salvó al punk. PiL

podcast.title: Musical Characteristics
podcast.body: Gothic rock is characterized by its dark and introspective nature, often utilizing minor keys. The sound frequently features sharp, brittle guitars and prominent reverb. The lyrical subject matter often incorporates religious and supernatural symbolism, described as gloomy, morbid, somber, and even vampiric, though Goths themselves are noted as being capable of happiness. "Yeah, the music is dark and introspective, often in a minor key, and can feature sharp brittle guitars and reverb."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origins Debate and Key Influences
podcast.body: The exact birth of gothic rock is difficult to pinpoint, as many artists were working in that direction, with some suggesting its genesis lies between Joy Division's *Unknown Pleasures* and *Closer*. While *Unknown Pleasures* provided an important foundation for the aesthetic and lyrical style of gothic rock, *Closer* was more crucial for defining its sound, and Bauhaus's nine-minute single "Bela Lugosi's Dead" is considered by many as the definitive starting point that truly launched the genre. "es muy difícil establecer cuando nace el rogótico porque teníamos a mucha gente trabajando en esa dirección y posible el nacimiento del rogótico esté aquí justo en el medio entre los dos album entre el no plecer y closer justo a la mitad apenas tres meses parrida tres meses para abajo salía lo que era verdaderamente lo que posiblemente se enlacimiento al rogótico que es ese single de nueve minutos de la banda bauja o de la lujo si sé que yo creo que sienta ya la base de lo que sigue al rogótico se seguiría definiendo aquí sobre todo en la parte del sonido se seguiría definiendo muchísimo lo que se da el rogótico posterior."

srcs.episode: Especial JOY DIVISION: 3. Closer y la muerte de Ian Curtis

podcast.title: Post-Punk Emergence (Late 1970s - Early 1980s)
podcast.body: Gothic rock emerged in the period immediately following 1970s punk rock, with its distinct development truly taking hold in the very late 1970s and early 1980s. Its sound diverged from punk, yet its existence was clearly facilitated by punk's preceding impact. "Gothic rock was one of the many genres that popped up in the era immediately after the punk rock of the 1970s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
